model_interpretation.claim: A warp-shuffle reduction followed by one shared exchange of four warp partials should reduce CTA-wide synchronization from the baseline tree’s repeated barriers to one per block. The recursive 128-element pass geometry stays fixed; 64-bit partials prevent overflow in intermediate groups when the valid final sum fits int. Added wide arithmetic and scratch traffic could offset the synchronization savings, so no whole-call speedup is assumed.

To isolate this axis, retain the baseline's recursive global pass structure, 128-thread mapping, and one input element per lane; do not change the global tile geometry. Preserve correct synchronization and exact summation for every valid input, including safe handling of intermediate sums, and obey the scratch, stream, allocation, and bounds constraints. Validate all required inputs and compare repeated full-call measurements against the baseline; report failures and do not assume a local-kernel improvement guarantees a whole-call improvement.
